reading: Joined by terms, a reading: BigCommerce's Settings APIs manage "the configuration settings that are exposed to merchants in their store control panel, such as the store's name and contact information" (BC-S-0263), with the scope store_v2_information, "View and modify store information and settings" (BC-S-0268), and the topic store/information/updated, fired "when changes are made to store settings" (BC-S-0269); they are Shopify's Store properties and shop/update (SH-S-0789, SH-S-1357) and Salla's store-settings scope (SA-S-1565). Strained: the concern also holds Storefront SEO (BC-S-0266), cited by domain E's part in CM-CNT-007, SEO, and left to it here; E also cites BC-S-0263 in CM-CNT-007 and CM-SFR-013 (search filters) and BC-S-0262 (the store's domain) in CM-SFR-008. Its Storefront Status (BC-S-0265) is cited here; what the status holds is not stated (see CM-ACC-007 and CM-ACC-009).

Joined by terms, a reading: BigCommerce's Contracting Entity, "the Commerce entity with which you are entering into this Agreement" (BC-S-0427), set by the merchant's country of residence (BC-S-0428 to BC-S-0432) with the governing law in the same table (BC-S-0426), is Shopify's Contracting Party, chosen by the store's billing address, with the Terms' governing law (SH-S-0001, SH-S-0010). The MSA's party clause (BC-S-0425), Germany's entity (BC-S-0433) and the US arbitration agreement (BC-S-0434) are the same clause's. Domain F's part cites BC-S-0428 and BC-S-0432 in CM-APP-011 as own-service, for the Extensions they name.

Joined on role, a reading: the MSA's Store Terms define a Store, which "can be individually configured with its own settings, payment methods, and 3rd party apps" (BC-S-0469), and make the merchant "solely responsible for your Stores and Your Materials" (BC-S-0471), as Shopify's Terms make the Store Owner responsible for the Account and allow one Store Owner per store (SH-S-0228, SH-S-0238). Strained: the rest of the concern is trust's. Commerce may remove Stores or Materials that violate laws or the Agreement (BC-S-0470), cited here in CM-ONB-002 and left to batch 2 for CM-TRU-009. The merchant must keep a privacy policy for Your Users (BC-S-0472), which domain E's part cites in CM-CNT-008, and must bind its users to an agreement releasing Commerce (BC-S-0473); both are left to batch 2 (CM-TRU-005 or CM-TRU-010). The reviewer may move the concern to CM-TRU-010.

Joined by terms: BigCommerce's Staff accounts, a plan line checked on all four plans (BC-S-0334), and its control panel users, which the GraphQL Account API creates, edits and deletes (BC-S-0333) under the scope account_users_write (BC-S-0335), are Shopify's staff accounts and Users (SH-S-0020, SH-S-1482). The same sentence is BC-C-055's (BC-S-0298, domain F), which F's part cites in CM-API-013.

Joined by terms: BigCommerce's Fees and Billing Terms (BC-I-0462), whose Fees "may include subscription fees, GMV overage fees, Open Payment Provider Fees" (BC-S-0184), payable in U.S. Dollars (BC-S-0188), are Shopify's Fees, in US dollars, with Subscription Fees billed in advance (SH-S-0033, SH-S-0034). Strained: the concern's plan side is cited in CM-PLN-001 (the GMV cap per plan, BC-S-0185, and automatic upgrades, BC-S-0186, BC-S-0187) and its Open Payment Provider Fee in CM-PLN-003, a different tree from CM-PLN-004's; its authorized payment method (BC-S-0191) and taxes (BC-S-0190) are cited in CM-PLN-004's children CM-PLN-005 and CM-PLN-007.

Joined by terms, a reading: BigCommerce "is a PCI DSS compliant service provider and validates annually all requirements (1-12)" under the title PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance (AOC) (BC-S-0169), and is responsible for the security of cardholder data to the extent it controls it (BC-S-0167); this is Shopify's Level 1 PCI DSS certification and its service provider Attestation of Compliance (SH-S-7202, SH-S-7481). Every statement of the concern (BC-S-0165 to BC-S-0171) is cited in CM-TRU-018's cell.

Joined by terms, a reading: BigCommerce's Storefront Cookie Consent API, to "specify shopper cookie consent preferences on BigCommerce-hosted storefronts" (BC-S-0215), and the control-panel setting that controls cookie consent (BC-S-0216, scoped to Catalyst storefronts), are Shopify's consent banner route and Customer Privacy API (SH-S-5031, SH-S-0835). All four statements are cited in CM-TRU-006's cell.

Joined on role, a reading: the MSA's Anti-Corruption, Export and Sanctions Compliance clause is the merchant's representations and covenants (BC-S-0435) to run a risk-based compliance programme with sanctions screenings of its Relevant Parties and customers (BC-S-0438) and to cooperate with Commerce on sanctions and ABAC laws (BC-S-0439); this is the role of Shopify's merchant who answers for its store and transactions and researches import and export laws (SH-S-0236, SH-S-0667), the laws the merchant must keep as the seller. Strained: its sanctions list (BC-S-0437) is also cited by batch 1 in CM-ACC-008, the countries the platform serves, where WooCommerce's sanctions concerns landed by M-084; and its termination for cause (BC-S-0436) is cited by batch 1 in CM-ONB-002. Both are outside CM-TRU-010's tree. The concern's own words are the merchant's compliance, not the platform's service area, so it lands here; the reviewer may weigh it against CM-ACC-008.

Joined by terms, a reading: under the Data Processing Addendum a Commerce Entity "shall act as Processor" on the customer's documented instructions (BC-S-0442), and for shoppers' information "The Merchant is the Controller" (BC-S-0443); this is Shopify's DPA, the merchant as Data Controller and Shopify as Data Processor (SH-S-0186). Strained: its Shopper requests (BC-S-0444) are cited in CM-TRU-007 (customer data requests), which is in CM-TRU-005's tree, not CM-TRU-013's.

Joined by terms, a reading: Commerce.com's Data Transfer section, that it may transfer, process and store Personal Data in the regions where it or its Subprocessors operate (BC-S-0445), under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (BC-S-0453), is Shopify's moving data geographically and its transfer agreements incorporating the Standard Contractual Clauses (SH-S-0637, SH-S-0643). Strained: Integrity and Stability (BC-S-0450, infrastructure replicated across availability zones) is domain G's: G's BigCommerce part cites it core in CM-OPS-001, platform reliability, and it is left there as "One thing, one domain" asks. The subprocessor rows BC-S-0446 to BC-S-0448 are cited here and in CM-TRU-015, a child of the same parent.

Joined by terms, a reading: Commerce.com's current Subprocessors, listed on its data-processors page (BC-S-0454), engaged under the DPA's general written authorization (BC-S-0456), are Shopify's Subprocessors and the merchant's objection to one (SH-S-0184, SH-S-0189). Strained: its uptime (BC-S-0455) is domain G's CM-OPS-001, where G's BigCommerce part cites it with its quality, and is left there; Hosting Services (BC-S-0457) is cited here as shows and by G as outside in CM-OPS-003, the store's hosting; its Backup Storage (BC-S-0459, the merchant's sole duty to back up its files and data on Commerce servers) is cited by no capability of domain A, and is a lead for G's CM-OPS-001 (see notes).

Joined by terms, a reading: the concern is BigCommerce's Acceptable Use Policy (its platform_terms; the legal agreement BC-I-0460), whose rule Lawful Purposes Only bars uses Commerce determines in its discretion to be unlawful, infringing, offensive or fraudulent (BC-S-0465); this is Shopify's Acceptable Use Policy and its main rule (SH-S-0166). Strained: its Highly Regulated Products statements (BC-S-0466, BC-S-0467, BC-S-0468) make the merchant solely responsible for the legality of its products, and are cited in CM-TRU-010, which is not in CM-TRU-009's tree. Gap: where acceptable use is enforced is "searched, not found" (BC-C-085/where).

Joined by terms, a reading: the Infringing Materials Protocol, under which Commerce may remove or block Your Materials on proper notice of copyright infringement (BC-S-0479), sent by the rights holder to its Intellectual Property Agent (BC-S-0480), is Shopify's notices of copyright infringement and its removal of infringing content (SH-S-7480, SH-S-7260). All four statements are cited in CM-TRU-011's cell.
